question: What is the main difference between an occupational disease and a sudden workplace injury?

options.A: It develops gradually over a long period
options.B: It cannot be prevented by using proper equipment
options.C: It only affects administrative hospital staff
options.D: It happens immediately following a major trauma

explanation: Occupational diseases are chronic conditions that build up over months or years of repeated exposure to workplace hazards, unlike sudden acute injuries. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why are midwives in clinical practice particularly exposed to health hazards at work?

options.A: They work exclusively in dry laboratory environments
options.B: They spend most of their working hours sitting at a desk
options.C: They have no contact with patients carrying infectious agents
options.D: They frequently handle sharp instruments and bodily fluids

explanation: Midwives face unique risks because their daily work involves close patient contact, handling sharps, and exposure to infectious fluids during deliveries. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which workplace safety action is considered the highest and most effective level in the hierarchy of controls?
explanation: Elimination sits at the very top of the hierarchy because completely removing the hazard stops any potential exposure from occurring in the first place. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h2)

question: How do engineering controls protect healthcare workers from workplace hazards?

options.A: By putting physical barriers between the worker and the hazard
options.B: By completely replacing the need for any workplace policies
options.C: By forcing staff to work longer shifts without taking breaks
options.D: By relying entirely on the worker remembering to wear gloves

explanation: Engineering controls use physical modifications, such as safety-engineered syringes or ventilation systems, to isolate staff from dangerous exposures. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h2)

question: A maternity ward replaces a harsh chemical disinfectant with a safer alternative. Which type of safety control is this?
explanation: Replacing a hazardous substance with a safer one falls under substitution, which is the second tier of the workplace control hierarchy. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of using a puncture-resistant sharps container?

options.A: To reduce the physical weight of general hospital rubbish
options.B: To prevent accidental needle-stick injuries among staff
options.C: To store clean sterile instruments ready for emergency use
options.D: To make clinical waste collection cheaper for the hospital

explanation: Puncture-resistant sharps containers are specifically engineered to contain used needles safely, preventing accidental injuries to midwives and cleaners. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT an administrative control in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Rotating nurses away from high-risk infectious isolation areas
options.B: Enforcing mandatory training sessions on infection prevention
options.C: Establishing strict institutional guidelines on maximum shift lengths
options.D: Installing a permanent ventilation extractor fan in the labor ward

explanation: Installing physical equipment like a ventilation fan is classified as an engineering control, not an administrative policy or work practice. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why are restricted shift lengths and scheduled rest breaks important for midwives?

options.A: They guarantee that hospitals spend less money on staff salaries
options.B: They reduce fatigue-related errors and accidental needle-pricks
options.C: They completely eliminate the biological risk of airborne diseases
options.D: They replace the need for wearing gloves during surgical repairs

explanation: Exhaustion impairs concentration and motor skills, increasing the likelihood of workplace accidents like needle-pricks; managing shifts helps protect staff. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h4)

question: Where does Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) sit within the standard hierarchy of workplace controls?

options.A: At the very bottom as the last line of defense
options.B: Right above elimination and before substitution
options.C: As an engineering control built into the building
options.D: At the very top as the most effective intervention

explanation: PPE is considered the least reliable control method because it relies entirely on proper human use and does not remove the hazard itself. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is a major limitation of relying only on PPE to protect healthcare workers from disease?

options.A: It makes administrative safety policies and training unnecessary
options.B: It completely removes the hazard from the surrounding environment
options.C: It automatically prevents all forms of physical fatigue and strain
options.D: If the item is damaged or worn incorrectly, exposure still occurs

explanation: PPE only protects if worn properly and consistently; any tear, improper removal, or lack of supply leaves the midwife vulnerable to infection. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of offering routine Hepatitis B immunizations to student midwives?

options.A: To build biological immunity against a common occupational hazard
options.B: To treat an active accidental needle-stick injury immediately
options.C: To replace the need for wearing gloves during deliveries
options.D: To eliminate the biological pathogen from the hospital air

explanation: Immunizations are a key component of medical surveillance and prevention, protecting workers before they encounter bloodborne pathogens. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h6)

question: How do baseline health screenings upon employment help healthcare workers?

options.A: They record pre-existing health statuses to track future work-related changes
options.B: They eliminate the need for engineering controls in the facility
options.C: They ensure that workers never contract any infectious disease
options.D: They serve as administrative punishment for failing safety exams

explanation: Baseline screenings provide a reference point for a worker's health, helping to determine if a later condition is work-related. [learn more](BMP126_U4_T3#BMP126_U4_T3_h6)
